vedic_reference.note: The name Peeyush is derived from the Sanskrit term पीयुष (pīyuṣ), which is derived from the Sanskrit term प्रजानातुर् (prajānātur), meaning 'one who is known to the people'. In Hindu mythology, the term पीयुष (pīyuṣ) is used to refer to the god Indra, who is considered to be the king of the gods and the god of rain, thunder, and the sky. The term is also used to refer to the god Vayu, who is the god of the wind and the brother of Indra.
